thread:
alex: Quick postmortem follow-up from the 03/15 latency spike. Short version: recurring GPU queueing on dedicated pools caused P95/P99 to breach and we burned through ~18% of the monthly error budget during the 20m window. Proposing a temporary SLO reset for the affected routes while remediation is done. Suggestions below.
chloe: Ack. Do we have a clear owner for the remediation runbook items? Also +1 on a temporary SLO reprieve if we can attach concrete timelines.
matt: I'll pick up the queueing root cause investigation and coordinate infra changes. Plan: dig into batch sizing + autoscaler thresholds today, propose changes by EOD. I can own the follow-up actions: infra change, canary, observability adjustments.
priya: I'll own dashboards & alert tuning. Action items: 1) add a per-pool backlog gauge to the SLO dashboard, 2) create a short-lived alert for queue depth > 80% with a 2m eval window, 3) add a burn-rate panel for the error budget. ETA: dashboard PR by tomorrow morning.
alex: Thanks. For the temporary SLO reset: propose increasing P95 latency SLO from 300ms -> 450ms for the affected routes for 48 hours starting when infra fix is deployed. Ops rationale: prevents paging for noisy regressions and gives team breathing room to validate changes. @chloe please confirm before we announce.
chloe: I support the 48h window if we tie it to the infra change rollout and automated rollback on increased error budget burn. Also prefer we scope it to the route tag "/generate" only.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-04. Linking postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-15-latency-spike
matt: Here are diagnostic commands I ran earlier. paste:
```
# top offending containers
kubectl top pod -l app=inference-pool -n dedicated-staging
# queue depth per worker
curl -s http://metrics.internal/pool/queue_depth | jq .
```
matt: Initial finding: autoscaler threshold for queue depth was set at 1200 requests; observed spikes to ~1800 which deferred extra workers by ~90s. Suspect conservative scale-up + large batch sizes causing head-of-line delay. I'll test reducing batch size from 32->16 and lower scale threshold to 800 in staging.
priya: I drafted the dashboard changes in the monitoring repo: PR #542. Panels: backlog gauge, burn-rate, top 10 offending models by p95. Linking in PR for review.
alex: Owner assignments recap: matt -> remediation/fix + rollout; priya -> dashboards & alerts; chloe -> signoff on SLO reset. Timeline: fix proposal by EOD today, staging canary within 24h, prod rollout + SLO reset window tied to rollout. Please add your GitHub handles to the postmortem so we can track.
chloe: I'll sign off once I see the canary metrics (p95 improvement and no regressing error budget). If ok, I'll submit the SLO change request to the compliance queue.
priya: small note: we should instrument KV cache hit rate on the same dashboard, saw some correlation in one trace.
alex: Good catch. Add that to the PR. Any blockers? If not, I'll file the SLO change doc and schedule a short blameless sync at 18:00 UTC to review canary results.
chloe: no blockers from security side.
matt: starting work now, will post updates in this thread. :rocket:
priya: will review PR and ping for quick review. :eyes:
ops-bot: Reminder: auto-rollback policy is enabled for canaries. If p95 > 500ms post-rollout for more than 10m, rollback will trigger automatically.
alex: Perfect — thanks everyone. Short follow-up checklist for the thread: [matt] infra PR, [priya] dashboard PR, [chloe] SLO change approval + announce, [alex] file SLO change doc + coordinate blameless sync. We'll reconvene after canary.
